title: Familiar Faces
summary: Weeks five and six. Friendship is mostly time: Théo goes back to the same café three times, and strangers become familiar faces. Includes the film night and the film-within-the-story. From this chapter on, faint watercolour appears inside lit areas only. Ends with 7 lights.

screens.image: A small corner café on a cobbled street, "Café du Pont" painted on the window. The street black; the café interior grey.
screens.caption: Café du Pont

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Café du Pont. It's not Lisa's café. That's the main thing Théo likes about it.

screens.image: Inside: a zinc counter, a barista with tattooed forearms (Nadia), an old man in a beret doing a crossword (Lucien).

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Visit one. Théo orders, sits by the window, and looks at {his|her|their} phone the whole time.

screens.image: Théo walking home, the café behind {him|her|them}.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Nobody talked to {him|her|them}. That's fine. That's not what visit one is for. Visit one is for being seen once.

screens.image: A friendship card slides in: Nadia's outline, a meter with marks: stranger / familiar face / acquaintance / casual friend / friend.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Here's a secret about friendship that nobody tells you: it's mostly hours. Around fifty hours together to become casual friends. Around two hundred to become close. Not magic. Not charm. Time.

screens.image: Calendar page flipping. Visit two. The café a little lighter.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Visit two, three days later. Same café. Same time. Lucien is in the same seat, doing the same crossword, swearing quietly at it.

screens.image: Lucien holding up his newspaper, pointing at a clue with a pencil.

words.speaker: Lucien
words.text: {Young man|Young lady|Young person}. Seven letters. 'What remains after the fire.' I have been stuck since Tuesday.

screens.image: Théo thinking.
Lucien delighted, writing.

words.speaker: Lucien
words.text: Cinders! Bravo. You may sit here on Thursdays.

screens.image: Lucien grumbling, then softening.

text.embers: Six letters. Hm. Never mind. Sit, sit, help me with the next one.
text.noidea: Hm. Never mind. Sit, sit, help me with the next one.

screens.image: Lucien and Théo bent over the crossword, a warm glow over the table; faint watercolour on the cups.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: They get four more clues. Lucien was a train driver for forty years. He has never once taken a holiday.

interaction.text: Lucien: train driver for forty years, never took a holiday. Thursday crosswords.

screens.image: Visit three. Théo at the door. Nadia looking up.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Visit three.

screens.image: Nadia smiling, already reaching for a cup. The café window glows.

words.speaker: Nadia
words.text: Allongé, no sugar?

screens.image: Close on Théo's face, surprised, the warm light on it.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: She remembered. Something small and stupid in Théo's chest lifts.

screens.image: Marie-Clo's notebook advice in a cream bubble: "Be interested in them."
screens.caption: "Be interested in them."

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Marie-Clo's homework. One real question.

options.label: "How did you end up working here?"

screens.image: Nadia leaning on the counter, showing a sketchbook of tattoo designs.

words.speaker: Nadia
words.text: I'm saving to open a tattoo studio. These are my designs. Don't laugh at the octopus.

screens.image: Théo laughing at the octopus. Nadia mock-offended.

text.thanks: Nadia smiles. Théo smiles back, and sits down.

interaction.text: Nadia: saving for her own tattoo studio. Sensitive about the octopus.

screens.image: Nadia pointing at a hand-drawn poster on the wall: a film reel, "CINÉ JEUDI".

words.speaker: Nadia
words.text: We do a film night Thursday. Old projector, bad chairs. Free. You should come.

interaction.prompt: How awkward do you think it'd be, 1 to 10?

screens.image: Thursday evening. The café dark except for a projector beam. A dozen people on mismatched chairs.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Thursday. Théo goes. {He|She|They} {sits|sits|sit} at the back, near the door, in case.

screens.image: The projector beam hitting a screen. The film begins (film panels have a different style: black-and-white, rounded corners like old film).

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Tonight's film is called The Keeper.

screens.image: FILM: a lighthouse on a rock, an old keeper climbing the spiral stairs.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: An old keeper lives alone on a lighthouse. Every night for thirty years, he lights the lamp.

screens.image: FILM: the keeper staring at an empty, dark sea.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: One winter, no ships come. Not one. He waits a week. A month.

screens.image: FILM: the keeper sitting in the dark, the lamp unlit, a bottle on the table.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: "Nobody is out there," he says. So he stops lighting the lamp.

screens.image: FILM: the sea in total darkness, then tiny lights far away: small boats, fishermen, lost in the dark.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: But the boats were there all along. Small ones, too small to see. They had been steering by his light for thirty years. Without it, they can't find their way home.

screens.image: FILM: the keeper climbing the stairs, lighting the lamp. The beam sweeps out. One by one, the little boats turn toward it.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: He climbs the stairs. He lights the lamp. One by one, the boats turn home.

screens.image: FILM: morning. Fishermen climbing up the rock with bread, fish, wine. The keeper at a full table.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: In the morning, they climb the rock to thank him. He had never once met them. They had always known him.

screens.image: Back in the café. Théo wiping {his|her|their} eyes. Two rows ahead, Lucien wiping his too.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Théo cries at the part with the boats. So does Lucien. Neither mentions it.

screens.image: After the film, people chatting in small groups; Théo standing at the edge holding a cup.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Afterwards, people talk in little groups. Théo stands at the edge, holding a cup like a shield.

screens.image: Nadia, Lucien and Théo by the counter.

words.speaker: Lucien
words.text: The keeper was an idiot. You don't stop lighting the lamp because you can't see anyone.

words.speaker: Nadia
words.text: That's the whole film, Lucien.

screens.image: Théo walking home along the river. Two small warm lights behind {him|her|them} in the café window.
A small chart drawn like a pencil sketch: prediction vs reality.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Théo guessed {before:film}. It was really {after:film}. Our brains are terrible at predicting this. They nearly always guess worse than it is.

screens.image: Light Map: the café window now glowing on the skyline, with faint watercolour.

words.speaker: narrator
words.text: Seven lights. One of them is a whole café.

screens.image: Quest card.

interaction.title: Three times
interaction.text: Go to your place three times in the next two weeks, same day and time if you can. You don't have to talk to anyone. Being seen counts.
